title: Professional 2D primitives + modify system: the genuinely usable AutoCAD-class drafting vocabulary
objective: Deliver the professional 2D drawing/editing system on the frozen CAD/BIM Product Architecture v1.0 (Issue #78; product requirements CAD-2D-001/002/003 of spec/cad-bim/requirements.md carried under platform requirement CAD-001): the CAD-2D-001 primitive vocabulary (ELLIPSE, SPLINE, POINT, RAY/XLINE, REGION on top of the existing LINE/POLYLINE/CIRCLE/ARC) and the CAD-2D-002 modify vocabulary (ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR, OFFSET, and the generalized TRIM/EXTEND with implied-all-edges Enter semantics, STRETCH, FILLET, CHAMFER, BREAK, JOIN, EXPLODE on top of the existing MOVE/COPY/ERASE), all operating on CANONICAL geometry through a shared engine-free 2D kernel (app/src/workspace/geometry: math, entities, spline, intersections, parameterization, transforms, fillet/chamfer, offset, edit-ops) behind a storage-convention bridge that unifies the COMPAT-CAD-001 drafting vocabulary and the canonical flat records into ONE geometry view; the CAD-2D-003 precision aids (nine object-snap modes with deterministic priority, ortho/polar constraints, grid snap, object-snap tracking, deterministic picking and window/crossing selection incl. sampled spline crossing) as the SAME shared module the App API precision queries expose; the additive entity.create/entity.modify App API commands with single atomic applyEdits revisions per operation; the additive prompt-engine extensions (entityPoint step kind where the pick location is semantic, option sub-prompts for OFFSET Through / FILLET Radius / CHAMFER distances, pick-derived angles, RAY/XLINE chainKeep, implied-all-edges Enter); the Web host workspace extension (canonical rendering, merged picking, previews, ribbon tools, properties, grips) and the equivalent Electron renderer extension; deterministic tests and CI proving semantic correctness, interaction parity, selection fidelity, associativity, determinism, Web/Electron parity and regression.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic correctness: every advertised primitive and modify operation computes exact canonical geometry with explicit typed failure behavior per command (deterministic kernel, LOCK-007 — malformed/degenerate inputs are rejected with stable codes, never silently repaired).

Interaction parity: every CAD-PARITY-003 command is reachable from the command line (names + aliases), the ribbon/tool palette and the keyboard map on BOTH hosts through the ONE shared command registry and prompt engine — no host-specific command implementations.

Selection fidelity: window/crossing, cycling, preselection and pick modifiers keep working (CAD-PARITY-002 regression) and cover the new entity vocabulary through the shared merged pick; grips cover the canonical flat-convention entities.

Associative behavior: modify operations operate on canonical geometry rather than UI approximations — the bridge loads BOTH storage conventions into ONE canonical view, every operation computes through the kernel and writes back one atomic revision (setProps full replacement so stale legacy fields never persist); REGION derived properties (area/perimeter/centroid) are recomputed server-side and forged values are rejected.

Determinism: identical command sequences produce identical entity ids, revisions, snap/pick results and persisted output on every host and every run (determinism double-runs are part of the test suite; the CAD-PARITY-002 parity fixture save sha stays intact).

Web/Electron parity: the same command script produces the same canonical result on both hosts — the Electron workspace smoke drives the REAL professional UI (19 steps: the 14-step CAD-PARITY-002 parity workflow unchanged + ELLIPSE exact, TRIM implied-all-edges with an entityPoint canvas pick, ROTATE 45° typed exact, ribbon drives all 18 new commands, canonical pick + properties) and asserts the SAME pinned parity fixture.

UI quality: professional CAD editor feel — command previews (ghost transforms, offset preview, hover emphasis), typed coordinate grammar, contextual prompts with option keywords, snap markers, live properties — browser-verified on the dev server (the same build surface CI validates).
Regression: all existing workflows stay green — 409 pre-existing app tests, the CAD-PARITY-002 web workspace smoke with the pinned parity fixture, and all ten Electron regression smokes.
non_goals: Layers/properties/style palettes beyond the existing surface (CAD-PARITY-004 scope).

Exact spline intersections (the typed kernel limitation is explicit: TRIM/EXTEND/BREAK targets and OFFSET sources exclude splines/ellipses/regions with typed declines; window-crossing selection approximates spline crossing deterministically through the fixed 32-sample polyline).
FILLET/CHAMFER circle-arc pairs (line-pair corners are exact; circle/arc pairs report the typed limitation) and the interactive polyline mode (available through entity.modify).
ROTATE/SCALE reference modes, COPY multiple-placement repeat and FILLET radius persistence across commands (typed coordinate input covers the geometry exactly; documented as future refinement).
Multi-point object-snap tracking acquisitions beyond the existing single-base tracking.
CIRCLE/ARC alternate input modes (2P/3P/diameter) — the primary center-based flows are unchanged and regression-pinned.
Architecture changes (Architecture v1.1 and the CAD/BIM Product Architecture v1.0 stay frozen; no protected path touched).
Approval or verification claim by implementation (the process stops at PR_OPEN for Architect review of the actual UI and workflow behavior).

transitions.failure_reason: (1) joinLines merges any collinear lines by min/max projection without requiring touching/overlap — disconnected lines with a gap are fabricated into one continuous line, violating the requirement that modify operations operate on canonical geometry without inventing geometry. (2) extendGeom's ARC start-side path searches CCW from the current start and reconstructs the arc from that hit — the start can move in the wrong direction and shorten or misorient the arc; directed regression tests for both picked ends and correct interval handling are required. Additionally the documented omissions (ROTATE/SCALE reference mode, advanced repeat/persistence behaviors) must be represented explicitly as supported/unsupported command behavior with typed failures rather than presented as complete parity.

decisions.rationale: Architect review of CAD-PARITY-003 / PR #79 (comment 5454974593): the frozen architecture remains sound and the CI/test evidence is strong, but two real semantic defects in the canonical geometry kernel must be fixed before approval. (1) joinLines accepts any collinear lines and takes the min/max projected endpoints — two lines with a gap become one longer line, fabricating geometry and violating the requirement that modify operations operate on canonical geometry without inventing geometry. (2) extendGeom's ARC start-side path searches CCW from the current start and reconstructs the arc from that hit, which can move the start in the wrong direction and shorten or misorient the arc. Additionally, the currently documented omissions (e.g. ROTATE/SCALE reference mode and advanced repeat/persistence behaviors) must be represented explicitly as supported/unsupported command behavior with typed failures rather than presented as complete parity. The formal GitHub REQUEST_CHANGES operation was rejected because the connected account is the PR author, so the review is recorded as the authoritative PR comment instead. No architecture change is required.
decisions.remediation_required: Fix the geometry semantics (JOIN must reject disconnected geometry; ARC EXTEND must use directed interval handling for both picked ends), add directed regression tests, rerun the complete 2D + regression + Web/Electron parity suite, update the governance evidence, and return PR #79 for review.

decisions.rationale: Architect re-review of CAD-PARITY-003 / PR #79 (comment 5455562484): the JOIN/ARC-EXTEND geometry remediation is accepted in principle and the 596-test/34-check green posture is strong, but the program-level CAD parity rule established after CAD-PARITY-002 requires every Web-facing parity sprint to be browser-verified against the exact deployed Vercel revision, not only a local dev server, and PR #79 explicitly stated no Vercel Preview was deployed. No further geometry changes were requested unless the deployed test exposed another defect.
